dial.summary: Six of eight macro indicators remain supportive as BTC dominance holds firm at 57.3% on a $2.28T total market cap — global liquidity trending higher at ~$103.2T, the 2s10s curve steepened to +45bps, manufacturing PMI at 55.6% confirms expansion, and stablecoin dominance compressed further to 13.2%; real yields at 2.39% remain the lone structural headwind with July CPI (August 12) as tomorrow's pivotal catalyst — a soft print could compress DFII10 below 2% and push DXY into supportive territory below 97.5, reinforcing the BTC Accumulation thesis.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: MacroMicro 4-bank aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) confirmed at $102,663.81B ($102.66T) for June 2026 — July 2026 global aggregate not yet published on MacroMicro as of August 11; US M2 (H.6 weekly) rose to $23.3T in July 2026 (up from $23.16T in June, +$0.14T, 29th consecutive monthly increase, +5.6% YoY), confirming continued global liquidity expansion; estimated global aggregate ~$103.2T as July central bank data is incorporated across all four banks; 4-week trend up: ~$102.7T (July 10 estimate, interpolated from June confirmed $102.66T) → ~$103.2T (Aug 11 estimate) = +$0.5T (~0.49%); status supportive (4-week uptrend confirmed; YoY growth remains positive; headwind condition — contracting YoY — not met).

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: July 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.6% (released August 3, 2026) remains the most recent reading — 2.3pp above June's 53.3%, highest since May 2022, seventh consecutive expansion month; August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI does not release until September 1, 2026; sub-indexes: Production 58.5%, New Orders 56.7%, Employment 52.8% (first factory employment expansion in 33 months), Prices Paid 71.1%; July NFP released August 7 at −23,000 (first monthly job loss in years, vs +80k consensus) — sharp deterioration reducing September rate-hike probability from 58% to ~30%, shifting the macro backdrop more dovish despite ISM strength; 4-week trend up: 53.3% (June) → 55.6% (July) = +2.3pp; status supportive (above 50 and rising; headwind thresholds <48 falling or >62 not met).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY recovered to 99.80 as of August 10–11, 2026 (rebounding from the August 10 low of 99.60 following the July NFP shock on August 7); DXY fell from ~101.39 in early July through August as the July NFP (−23,000, August 7) drove rate-cut repricing and reduced the dollar's yield advantage; the partial recovery on August 10–11 reflects some unwind of NFP-driven positioning ahead of the July CPI print (August 12); 4-week trend: DXY ~101.39 (July 10 area) → 99.80 (Aug 11) = −1.57%, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; trend down; status NEUTRAL per ICE DXY spot threshold (99.80 is above the 97.5 supportive boundary but below the 100 headwind boundary, sitting near the upper edge of the neutral band); July CPI (Aug 12) is the primary directional catalyst — a sub-2.8% headline print could accelerate DXY toward 97.5 (supportive).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: DFII10 (10-year TIPS real yield) at 2.39% as of August 7, 2026 (most recent confirmed post-NFP close; July 23 TIPS auction cleared at 2.438%, July 29 close 2.41%, post-NFP Aug 7 eased to 2.39% as nominal yields fell ~7bps on the jobs shock); no new H.15 data available for August 10–11 as of this run (H.15 releases end-of-day); 4-week trend up: ~2.18% (July 10 estimate) → 2.39% (Aug 7) = +21bps, well above the 5bps flat threshold; status headwind (above the 2% absolute threshold — sole remaining structural headwind; September FOMC hike probability dropped to ~30%; July CPI (Aug 12) is the primary real-yield compression catalyst — a soft print combined with continued labor softening could bring DFII10 below 2.0%).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: August 10–11, 2026: DGS10 ~4.65%, DGS2 ~4.20%, spread +0.45% (+45bps); slight compression of 1bp from the August 7 post-NFP peak of +46bps as the short end (2Y at 4.20%) held firm while the 10Y remained at 4.65%; 4-week comparison: July 10 spread ~+0.35% (+35bps) → Aug 11 +0.45% (+45bps) = +10bps steepening, above the 5bps flat threshold — trend up; status SUPPORTIVE (curve positive at +45bps AND steepening on a 4-week basis); July CPI (Aug 12) and FOMC Minutes (Aug 19) are the next curve catalysts — a soft CPI would compress the 2Y further and deepen steepening; Jackson Hole (Aug 27–29) is the subsequent major signal.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL (H.4.1): $6,748,567M ($6.75T) confirmed for week ending August 5, 2026 (H.4.1 released August 7) — up $8B from week ending July 29 ($6,741B); next H.4.1 covering week ending August 12 releases August 13 (no new data available as of August 11); 4-week trend flat: ~$6,720B (July 8 estimate) → $6,749B (Aug 5 confirmed) = +$29B (+0.43%), within the 0.5% flat threshold; status supportive (balance sheet holding at post-2022 plateau; no aggressive QT with rising overnight rates; July 29 FOMC held at 3.50–3.75%, 9-3 vote).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: Live funding rate data inaccessible — CoinGlass blocked by network egress proxy; value carried forward at +0.004%/8h from last accessible exchange-level data (Binance BTC perpetual ~0.005%, Bybit ~0% in late July 2026); contextual signals as of August 11, 2026: BTC dominance at 57.3% (stable), total crypto market cap $2.28T, stablecoin dominance falling to 13.2%; the July NFP shock (−23,000, August 7) reduced September rate-hike probability to ~30%, a macro backdrop consistent with spot accumulation rather than leveraged long speculation; near-zero positive funding well below the 0.04%/8h overheating threshold; 30-day trend down (from ~+0.006%/8h in late June toward near-zero); status supportive (near-zero funding signals healthy long bias without leverage overheating).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$302B (USDT ~$186B, USDC ~$75B, balance in USDS/DAI/PYUSD) as of August 11, 2026; total crypto market cap $2.28T; stablecoin dominance $302B / $2.28T ≈ 13.2% — compressing slightly from 13.3% on August 10 as stablecoin supply held flat while total market cap edged up; BTC dominance at 57.3% confirms capital continues to favor BTC; 30-day trend down: ~14.3% (July 10 estimate) → 13.2% (Aug 11) = −1.1pp compression as capital rotated from stablecoins into risk assets over 30 days; status supportive (falling on 30-day basis; headwind threshold requires rising dominance WHILE TOTAL crypto is also rising — not met since dominance fell net over 30 days as capital deployed into BTC).

upcoming.title: CPI (July 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Consumer Price Index for July 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — the single most critical data point of the week, arriving five days after July NFP's shock −23,000 print; real yields at 2.39% (headwind) and DXY at 99.80 (neutral, near upper band) make a soft CPI the primary catalyst for real-yield compression and a potential DXY break below 97.5; ISM Prices Paid elevated in Manufacturing (71.1%), signaling pipeline pressure; oil-price moderation provides a deflationary offset in the energy component; a soft July CPI (headline <2.8%, core <3.0%) would accelerate the September rate-cut debate already energized by the NFP miss and is the principal near-term catalyst for the BTC Accumulation thesis.

upcoming.title: PPI (July 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Producer Price Index for July 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — released one day after July CPI (August 12); PPI feeds directly into core PCE components (healthcare and financial services); ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid at 71.1% signals upstream pipeline pressure, but oil-price moderation may provide a significant goods PPI offset; a soft PPI would reinforce the disinflation + labor-softening combination that strengthens the September rate-cut case; a hot PPI — particularly in trade services or healthcare — would signal pipeline risks not captured in headline CPI.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended August 8, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for the week ending August 8, 2026 — the first weekly labor read following July NFP's shock −23,000 print (August 7); prior weeks showed low claims (~197–225k); if claims begin rising here, it would corroborate the NFP deterioration and significantly increase September rate-cut probability; released alongside July PPI — a claims + PPI surprise combination in either direction amplifies the market reaction.

upcoming.title: Retail Sales (July 2026)
upcoming.note: US Census Bureau Advance Monthly Retail Sales for July 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — key growth gauge arriving after the NFP shock (Aug 7), CPI (Aug 12), and PPI (Aug 13); June 2026 retail sales rose 0.2% MoM, +6.7% YoY; a miss in retail sales on top of the labor deterioration would compound soft-landing → hard-landing concerns; a strong retail print (>0.4% MoM) would confirm consumer resilience despite the labor miss and reinforce BTC Accumulation.

upcoming.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (August 2026 preliminary)
upcoming.note: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment preliminary for August 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — first sentiment read post July NFP (Aug 7) and post July CPI (Aug 12); July 2026 UMich came in at 54.4 (highest since February 2026); the 5-year inflation expectation component is particularly watched given ISM Prices Paid elevated in Manufacturing (71.1%); oil-price moderation could reduce 1-year inflation expectations and lift headline sentiment; a sentiment drop alongside the negative NFP would compound recession-risk signals.

upcoming.title: Empire State Manufacturing Index (August 2026)
upcoming.note: NY Federal Reserve Empire State Manufacturing Survey for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — first August manufacturing regional read, cross-checking whether the July ISM Manufacturing surge to 55.6% (4-year high) extended into August and survived the July labor market shock (−23,000 NFP, August 7); a reading above zero (expansion) alongside ISM strength would confirm geographic breadth; released at the start of the pivotal August 17–19 data cluster culminating in FOMC Minutes (Aug 19).

upcoming.title: Housing Starts & Building Permits (July 2026)
upcoming.note: US Census Bureau Housing Starts and Building Permits for July 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — released one day ahead of FOMC Minutes (Aug 19); housing remains sensitive to real yields (DFII10 at 2.39%, above the 2% headwind threshold constraining mortgage affordability); any improvement in July housing data after the nominal yield decline post-NFP would signal that the real-yield headwind is beginning to ease; DFII10 below 2.0% remains the key catalyst for a sustained housing recovery.
